messages:
Amy Chen: Quick design review — private setup wizard's IP/CIDR step copy is confusing for customers trying to whitelist egress. copying what users see: 
Jake Ortiz: ah yep saw a support ticket this morning. can you paste the exact copy? :eyes:
Amy Chen: Current: 

  'Enter IP ranges allowed to reach your private deployment. Separate multiple ranges with commas.'

  Folks misinterpret 'reach' as inbound only. also the example is missing /mask which leads to sloppy entries.
Marta Ivanova: +1 on ambiguity. Proposal: change to microcopy that explains direction and shows validated example. Draft: 

  'Add outbound CIDR ranges (IPv4) customers will allow our control-plane to reach. Use CIDR notation, e.g. `192.168.0.0/24`. Separate ranges with commas or press Enter.'

  Also suggest an inline helper link 'What is CIDR?' for novices and visible example below the input.
Samir Patel: Technically we accept both comma and newline separated entries. backend already normalizes. For validation we should run a quick CIDR parse and show inline errors per line. regex we use server-side: `^((25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|[01]?\d?\d)(\.|$)){4}/(3[0-2]|[12]?\d)$` 
Ira Gomez: We need to keep copy short for smaller screens. Maybe two-line helper: one sentence + single example inline. Also call out 'egress' vs 'ingress' — product prefers 'outbound'/'inbound' terms?
Marta Ivanova: Product typically uses 'outbound'/'inbound' in docs but UI uses conversational copy. Suggest: 

  'Enter the outbound IP ranges we can use to communicate with your VPC (CIDR format). Example: `10.0.0.0/16`.'

  Accessibility: label should be `<label for=>Outbound IP ranges (CIDR)`. Input should have `aria-describedby` pointing to helper text and `aria-invalid` on errors. Keyboard: ensure Tab lands on example link, then on Add button.
Amy Chen: UX nit: when validation fails, highlight the specific bad range and keep focus in the input so keyboard users can fix without hunting. error state message: 'Invalid CIDR: `192.168.1.500/24` — use IPv4 CIDR (e.g. 192.168.0.0/24)'.
Samir Patel: agree. Implementation note: we'll return structured error mapping like `[{index:0, error:"invalid_cidr"}]` but UI only needs to surface string. We'll add a small copy for batch errors: 'One or more ranges look invalid — click to view details.'
Jake Ortiz: Layout debate: do we show the example inline inside the placeholder or as persistent helper text beneath? my vote: persistent helper text. Placeholders disappear and aren't accessible.
Marta Ivanova: persistent helper text + visually subdued example. Contrast check: helper text must meet AA contrast with background. I'll run a check but aim >4.5:1 for any interactive text.
Ira Gomez: Product ask: add a small 'Test connectivity' link after the input that triggers our preflight check and shows a toaster. That needs copy too: 'Test outbound connectivity' -> will run preflight and show which ranges are reachable.
Samir Patel: preflight will take ~10s. We should disable the button while running and use `aria-busy="true"`. Also return per-range status (reachable/unreachable) so we can mark with green/red badges.
Amy Chen: final microcopy suggestion for the input area: 

  Label: 'Outbound IP ranges (CIDR)'
  Helper: 'CIDR format; comma or newline separated. Example: 192.168.0.0/24.'
  Error: 'Invalid CIDR at position 2 — see details.'

  Small accessibility note in UI doc: 'Ensure focus remains on the input and error summary is announced via `role=alert`.'
Jake Ortiz: looks good. I'll mock up the new UX and push a screenshot later. @Marta can you confirm color tokens for helper text and error states? :thumbsup:
Marta Ivanova: will confirm contrast tokens and push updated figma frame by EOD. will include keyboard flow and aria copy.
setup-bot: Preflight run queued for 1779999999 — will post results in thread when complete.
Amy Chen: thanks all — aim to land copy + accessibility changes in next sprint. :rocket:
